title: The Circle of Fifths — Basics
intro: Welcome to Tritonet! In this lesson you will explore the Circle of Fifths and understand how keys relate to each other. The Tritonet circle shows all 12 tones. Let's begin.

steps.text: Look at the Tritonet circle. Each position represents a semitone. The highlighted position is the current root note (key center). Press any note on the circle to select a new key.
steps.hint: You can also press keys 1–6 on your keyboard to trigger chords.

steps.text: The 'anchor' (the fixed point on the circle) determines the relationship between the root and the scale. Try moving the anchor by clicking the inner ring segments.
steps.hint: The anchor controls whether you hear a major, minor, or modal sound.

steps.text: Now switch to the Calculator view using the view selector at the bottom of the canvas. This view shows note names around the circle, making it easier to read intervals.
Great! Try playing the same chord in a few different keys. Notice how the visual pattern stays the same — only the names change. This is the power of the Tritonet system.
steps.hint: Move the root by clicking different positions on the outer ring.

steps.text: Lesson complete! You have explored the basics of the Tritonet interface. Next: try the Mundana (Zodiac) view for an astronomical perspective on harmony.
